issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently specifies the parameter type for addGuestStudents: one place (line 50) says addGuestStudents(String) while the UML and the solution implementation declare addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch can confuse students about the correct signature to implement and will cause failures when matching the provided solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type for addGuestStudents consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Preferably update the problem statement text at line 50 to declare addGuestStudents(int) (and update any descriptive text/examples accordingly) so it matches the UML and the solution. Alternatively, if a String parameter was intended, update the UML, template TODO, and solution to use String instead.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to implement addGuestStudents(String) (parameter type String), whereas the UML diagram and the solution implementation define addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch between the described method signature and the intended/implemented signature creates confusion about the expected parameter type and may lead students to implement the wrong signature or struggle to match tests and UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent with the UML and solution by changing the textual task to request addGuestStudents(int) (i.e., accept an int parameter). Alternatively, update the UML and solution to use String consistently if String was intended — but prefer using int for number-of-students parameters.
